text:
Close the 340K proxy-cache cliff leak (R20a-c)

Problem (2027-01-09 cache round 5, HIGH): post-R12, 47 requests still crossed the ~340K litellm proxy cache ceiling at 16.3% hit (340-400K bucket: 83.7% resets; daily maxP reaches 408,956). R13 (fill_rate 0.3 + the 340K ceiling minus a 32,768 margin → effective trigger ~300K on 1M-window GLM endpoints) did NOT prevent over-cliff prompts.

Root cause (three stacked gaps, code-verified):
1. Rule-4 skip: when the conversation ends in an open tool loop spanning back to messages[1] (a long single-turn tool run — exactly where context grows fastest), summary_cut_index retreats the cut to the loop start and summarize returns messages UNCHANGED (src/agent/context.rs:262-264, 336-338, 437-485); maybe_compact falls through and the request is sent at full size.
2. No send-gate: when compaction runs but cannot shrink below the threshold, the code explicitly continues (src/agent/turn.rs:1743-1750 — "Still over: the kept-verbatim tail dominates..."); the 5-attempt budget aborts only on the 5th attempt, so up to 4 over-cliff requests go out per turn, and the next turn resets the budget.
3. Tokenizer drift: the trigger counts cl100k BPE tokens; the provider counts GLM tokens (~10% higher on code-heavy content) — a 300K-cl100k conversation can be 330-345K provider tokens, and one iteration's tool results plus GLM reasoning echo (policy: never strip) jumps past the trigger between checks.

Fix instructions (R20, three parts):
a. Send-gate at the cliff (src/agent/turn.rs maybe_compact ~:1660-1760): when the pre-request count is still over the proxy ceiling after the compaction attempts, do NOT send the full prompt — either (i) allow under-pressure historical-reasoning stripping for GLM as a cliff-pressure exception (the under_pressure machinery exists at src/provider/openai/request.rs:54 and DeepSeek uses it; GLM's never-strip policy blocks it — src/provider/policy.rs), or (ii) fail the turn fast with an actionable error instead of burning up to 4 over-cliff requests.
b. Trigger margin for 1M-window endpoints (src/config/general.rs:334/343 defaults; src/agent/context.rs:151-163 trigger math): lower the effective trigger to ~280K (fill 0.28 for 1M windows, or ceiling 320K) so tokenizer drift plus one tool batch cannot jump past the cliff.
c. Rule-4 fast-fail signal: when summarize no-ops because the open tool loop spans the conversation AND the count is over the ceiling, return a "skipped: open loop" signal from summarize/summarize_with_interrupt (src/agent/context.rs:262-264, 336-338) so maybe_compact surfaces "context over the proxy cache ceiling inside an open tool loop — finish or interrupt the tool run" immediately instead of silently re-sending.

Acceptance: a regression test where a conversation over the ceiling inside an open tool loop fails fast (or strips under pressure) instead of sending >340K; no post-fix request_stats row exceeds the ceiling (verify via the aggregates extraction); cargo test --workspace green with the existing compaction tests updated to the new behavior.

Pointers: .coding/reviews/2026-09-09-cache-hit-5-review.md (HIGH-1, R20); .coding/analysis/cache-hit-5-aggregates.txt (A3/A4 buckets); executive summary BUG 4.
note: Closed 2026-11-11 (lead clean-up): obsolete. The LiteLLM proxy-cache ceiling was removed from compaction triggering, and no configured endpoint runs through a LiteLLM proxy any more (DeepSeek, Ollama Cloud, Kimi).

text:
Move API keys to the OS keychain

Problem (2027-01-09 security review, LOW, optional): endpoint API keys sit plaintext at rest (endpoints.toml / ~/.mnemo/keys.toml) — DACL-restricted on Windows, 0600 on Unix. An OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain) would tighten at-rest storage. Worthwhile AFTER the .git/ sandbox-escape item lands (that one is the actual escape hatch).

Fix instructions:
1. Add an optional keychain backend for endpoint secrets: on load, if a key is referenced as keychain:<name>, fetch it from the OS store (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain via the `keyring` crate or equivalent) instead of the file.
2. Keep file-based keys working (default unchanged — no forced migration); add a settings action to migrate a key into the keychain.
3. Multi-platform neutrality: the crate must support both Windows and macOS (the project's review expectation) — `keyring` v3 does.
4. Tests: a mocked keyring backend round-trip; config load with keychain: references; cargo test green on both platforms.

Acceptance: a key stored in the OS keychain is used for requests with no plaintext on disk; file keys still work; cargo test --workspace green.

Pointers: .coding/reviews/2026-09-09-security-review.md (LOW-3).
note: Decided 2026-11-11: keep, deferred — do it as its own plan after Mnemo1 is retired, so the key storage changes in one settings surface (Mnemo2 Endpoints) instead of two.

Deletion hygiene: pre-flight import-orphan check before the battery

Symptom (2027-01-14, job 2c step 2c.4, branch wt/mnemo): deleting `SteeringStats::shared()` (src/agent/steering_stats.rs :445-452, the G4 de-globalization) orphaned TWO imports one at a time — `OnceLock` (caught pre-build by a literal search probe) and then `Arc` (missed by that same probe because it was only removed from the use statement's tail, not checked for remaining use sites; caught solely by the battery: `error: unused import: Arc` at src/agent/steering_stats.rs :45). Under #![deny(warnings)] (both crate roots) each orphan is a hard build failure — two full cargo cycles were burned on a mechanically predictable failure. Repro: delete any fn that is an import's sole remaining user and run cargo test -p mnemo.

Fix direction: land the discipline where edits are governed — amend the project constitution's Code style section (agent.md at the repo root, "## Code style") with a deletion-hygiene rule: after any deletion edit, for EVERY symbol named in the touched files' `use` statements, run a literal search (glob the file, engine: index) for remaining use sites BEFORE the first battery run, and trim every orphaned import in the same edit — one search pass replaces N build cycles. Keep it to one short paragraph, style matching the neighboring bullets.

Acceptance: agent.md's Code style section carries the rule; the next deletion on this repo lands with zero orphan-import build cycles; no behavior changes anywhere (documentation-only change; cargo test still green trivially).

text:
Edit path: anchor-by-read-reference — kill post-compaction re-reads

Symptom (2027-01-14, Mnemo wt/mnemo, job 2c steps 2c.3-2c.5): file_edit requires the EXACT verbatim old_string, so every edit target must have been read in-context; when context compaction drops the verbatim bytes (it keeps summaries, not bytes), every pending edit anchor gets re-read — ~10 re-reads in one afternoon (brain.rs regions, workspace.rs, dispatch approval branch, spawn_agent.rs, policy.rs). Compounding: an oversized read batch auto-archives, and expand_result on it RE-ARCHIVED (the escape hatch failed), forcing fresh small slices instead.

Fix direction: anchor-by-read-reference in the edit tools — read_files already returns line-stamped content per file; give file_edit (and multi_edit's anchor items) an alternative anchor form {from_read: <read-result-id>, lines: [start, end], new_string} validated server-side against the CURRENT file bytes at those lines (any drift = hard fail, forcing a fresh read — never a silent mismatch). The verbatim anchor blob then never needs to live in the model's context; compaction becomes harmless to the edit path. Files: the read tool (src/tool/agent/ files — the read_files implementation), the edit tool (file_edit/multi_edit ops), their schemas. Keep the existing old_string form as-is (default); the reference form is additive.

Acceptance: (1) an edit whose anchor is a line-range reference to a prior read applies cleanly when the file is unchanged; (2) it hard-fails with a clear drift error when the file changed since the read (never a fuzzy apply); (3) a post-compaction session can resume an interrupted edit sequence without re-reading unchanged files; regression tests red-first per constitution; cargo test -p mnemo green.

Pointers: same subsystem family as backlog c439dda0 (search-tool perf) and 1ead68c3 (deletion hygiene) — the agent-edit-path efficiency series; HOW memory 9cc7e643 (search discipline). Kind=implementation; this repo is the tool's own codebase.

text:
Tool-argument decode errors: echo received bytes for one-shot recovery

Problem (2027-01-17, wt/mnemo, job 3a.6/3a.8): truncated/malformed tool-call argument payloads (model emission decay — the documented 2026-12-20 bug) reject with bare messages ("ops is required", schema-violation text) that do NOT show what the executor actually received. The agent blind-retries the identical payload, fails identically, and the harness correction loop fires (observed: two identical timeout corrections + repeated "ops is required" rejections on ~2.5-4 KB multi_edit/file_edit payloads; each costs a full round-trip).

Sites (verify first): the tool-argument decode + schema validation producers of "[tool error] ... is required" under src/tool/ and src/agent/dispatch.rs; the malformed-JSON rejection path for arguments. Do NOT regress src/tool/agent/edit_ops.rs:186/:199 — its messages are pinned by tests (backlog 08d2125d's landing; .coding/knowledge/spec/2027-01-11-emission-artifact-guard-per-op-delta-attribution.md).

Fix direction: on any argument decode/schema failure, the error the model sees should carry: (1) the failure kind (JSON parse vs schema field), (2) the byte offset plus a ~120-char received-tail around the break, (3) the named missing/unexpected field, (4) the remedy line (re-emit smaller / chunk / file_write full-file). Add "received N bytes" so truncation is self-evident — never leave a rejection blind-retryable.

Acceptance: unit tests feeding a deliberately truncated arguments JSON (mid-string AND mid-brace) assert the error names offset/tail + missing field; the pinned edit_ops substring tests stay green; full battery (cargo test -p mnemo; --features browser,embeddings; --workspace).

Related: .coding/knowledge/bug/2026-12-20-code-bearing-tool-payload-emissions-degrade-unde.md (root cause), backlog 08d2125d (the landed artifact guard — complementary).

text:
Persistent session context — durable resume without loss

The agent session's CONTEXT (the transcript + the resume-relevant session state) lives in memory only: a shutdown loses the conversation unless the caller exported a transcript themselves. Durable today: plan files (.coding/plans/<id>.md — the crash-resumption doc) and memory_write facts; NOT durable: the conversation and the spawn settings. The resume seam already exists but nothing persists to it — a caller must build `SpawnOptions { resume: Some(Transcript { messages }) }` (src/headless/types.rs) by hand and thread the same model/permissions/limits to reconstruct the session.

Problem to solve: with the option ON, every session durably snapshots at turn boundaries + park/end so ANY point is resumable without loss; with the option OFF, zero new disk writes and today's behavior is byte-identical.

Fix direction:
(1) Config option `persist_context` (default false — behavior-preserving) in the [general] section, src/config/general.rs (follow the compaction_survival pattern around :776), surfaced as a toggle in the GUI options dialog (the Settings pages + the config IPC).
(2) Persistence hook at turn end / park / session end: serialize Transcript + the resume state (model, permissions, limits, host_tools specs, external_policy spec) into the state dir (e.g. <state>/sessions/<session-id>.json) via the existing export machinery — `AgentSession::export_conversation` + `snapshot()` (src/headless/session.rs; §5.9.5 snapshot/pending in .coding/design/headless-free-agent.md).
(3) An Engine-side restore surface (e.g. `Engine::saved_sessions()` / `Engine::resume_session(id)`) that rebuilds SpawnOptions from the snapshot and spawns with `resume: Some(...)` — the initial_messages threading already exists in spawn_agent_shared (src/host/runtime.rs:73-289).
(4) Multi-platform: pure Rust + the existing config/IPC surfaces — no platform-specific paths (the state dir comes from Workspace.state_dir).

Acceptance criteria:
- Scripted-provider integration test (tests/integration/headless_kernel.rs pattern — RecordingLlm + opts(Workspace, cfg)): with the option on, run a turn, DROP the engine, start a fresh engine on the same state dir, resume the saved session, and assert the model's first request carries the prior messages + the spawn settings round-trip.
- With the option off: no new files appear under the state dir and all existing tests stay green.
- The toggle is visible in the options dialog and takes effect for NEW sessions (documented).
- Full workspace battery green (cargo test, exit 0, zero warnings under #![deny(warnings)]).

Pointers: memory "PLAN: Job 3c resume — D3 mid-step" (the manual state-save pattern this automates); master spec .coding/design/headless-free-agent.md §5.9.5 + §5.3 (resume); the transcript export (AgentSession::export_conversation) and spawn threading (src/host/runtime.rs:73-289).

text:
Second-instance warning survives shutdown

Problem (user-reported this session; the SECOND live report on this warning — the first, 2027-01-15 "it had switched away", is recorded in SPEC .coding/knowledge/spec/2027-01-11-same-project-instance-warning-is-a-launch-time-s.md): closing mnemo down does not clean up the "another instance of mnemo is running on this project" warning. Repro: (1) launch instance A on a project, launch instance B on the same project (B shows the warning dialog); close A — B's dialog stays on screen, still claiming an instance is working on the project; (2) on clean exit nothing removes <project>/.coding/instance.json, so a stale marker can later warn again when Windows recycles the dead pid to a live process.

Root cause (per the SPEC): <project>/.coding/instance.json {pid, started_at} is written ONLY at launch (src-tauri/src/main.rs:328-344; sole writer InstanceMarker::write src-tauri/src/instance_marker.rs:49) — nothing clears or updates it on app exit or project switch-away. The conflict is computed ONCE at startup (conflict_for src-tauri/src/instance_marker.rs:69 + instance_pid_alive src-tauri/src/startup.rs:115) -> runtime ctx (src-tauri/src/ipc/state.rs:155) -> StartupSnapshot -> frontend state (frontend/src/App.tsx:261); the dialog (App.tsx:731) renders while non-null, never re-evaluated, never retracted. It warns, does not lock.

Fix direction: (1) src-tauri: on clean exit (app exit + the project-switch restart path src-tauri/src/ipc/projects.rs:201) remove <project>/.coding/instance.json ONLY when the stored marker still names this process (read_marker + pid == std::process::id() guard before delete — last-writer-wins means a newer incumbent must be preserved); best-effort, never block exit; add the removal helper in src-tauri/src/instance_marker.rs with unit tests in its mod tests. (2) frontend: re-evaluate the conflict while the dialog is visible (liveness re-check on an interval/focus) and retract once the pid is dead; reword the dialog copy to "launched on this project (PID n, HH:MM)" per the SPEC — never assert current occupancy.

Acceptance: closing the warned-about instance retracts the surviving instance's warning without restart; after a clean exit the marker file is gone when the exiting instance was the last writer; crash re-launch still ignores its own stale marker; cargo test green with the new unit tests.

Related: SPEC .coding/knowledge/spec/2027-01-11-same-project-instance-warning-is-a-launch-time-s.md (mechanism + fix direction), SPEC 2027-01-11-per-instance-webview2-udfs-same-project-conflict.md, plan 5ce69497 (merged 5b18497), review .coding/reviews/2026-09-13-5ce69497-webview-udf-per-instance-review.md (pid-recycling residual).

PROBLEM / WHY IT SPLIT: two blockers found by the D5 probe (2026-10-13, tree 5d97bc1): (1) `Engine::brain()` is pub(crate) (src/headless/engine.rs:138) — an Engine constructed app-side builds its OWN brain, so "IpcState holds an Engine" as specced forks the app into two brain halves sharing only the memory store (the D7 `.memory_store(Arc<dyn MemoryStoreTrait>)` seam, engine.rs:113); doing it right needs a NEW design decision — either a pub brain-injection seam on EngineBuilder (mirroring .memory_store/.shared_resources) or a deliberate two-lane architecture doc. (2) console.rs is 2,733 lines with its own AgentManager/AgentLoopFactory/HostRuntime loop wiring (:33-41, :1180, :1216, :1497-1501) — the rebuild alone exceeds the ~3k-line split threshold.

EXACT SEAMS (probed, verified 2026-10-13): the GUI Ready branch builds the brain at src-tauri/src/main.rs:393 (build_brain) with the handles at :459-474 (brain.own_memory_store: Option<Arc<MemoryStore>> — the concrete store for the .memory_store coercion; brain.workspace.root; the brain.config tokio-Mutex Arc — NOT reachable from an Engine today; block_on precedent at :462); the console path builds its own at console.rs:1180. EngineOptions wants { workspace: Workspace{root, state_dir, require_git}, config_dir: Option<PathBuf>, permissions, memory: MemoryBackend (overridden by .memory_store), index_codegraph, require_git, auto_install_embedder } (src/headless/types.rs:60-98). The public surface an Engine would serve app-side: AgentSession spawns (engine.spawn(SpawnOptions)), Setup::for_engine live-apply (job 4 D9 F2), MemoryApi/CodegraphApi/TraceApi/EngineStats (headless re-exports, src/headless/mod.rs:24-56).

FIX DIRECTION: (a) design + land the brain-share seam (pub EngineBuilder injection or a documented two-lane decision — spec a step file first, the job-5 pattern); (b) construct the Engine in main.rs's Ready branch sharing the app's store + config dir; hold it in IpcState (src-tauri/src/ipc/state.rs:47 — add `pub engine: Option<mnemo::headless::Engine>` + a getter); (c) route ONE proving consumer (a headless engine-status command via engine.stats(), or the classifier Setup::for_engine live-apply in ipc/laya.rs); (d) the console rebuild onto Engine/AgentSession in slices with the battery per chunk.

ACCEPTANCE: boundary scan stays green (tests/boundary.rs::tauri_uses_only_public_api — no mnemo::agent::/runtime::/host:: paths, the facade at src/lib.rs covers any new types); cargo test --workspace exit 0 (the app crate compiles); the GUI + console behave as before (the 83 integration fixtures + the IPC contract fixtures green); the row-35 guard (2a goldens) green.

text:
create_plan UX: cut the two first-call failure modes (steps-as-string, gate evidence phrasing)

Problem (2027-01-15, dispatching backlog c439dda0 -> plan 89bbd2a9): two consecutive create_plan rejections before the plan landed — each costs a full re-emit of a multi-KB call and a recovery round.

(1) steps-as-string: the `steps` argument went out as a JSON-encoded STRING instead of a native array. The error ("an argument must be a sequence, not a string. Please check each parameter's type against the tool's schema", rendered at src/tool/error_message.rs:87) names NEITHER the offending parameter NOR the expected shape — the agent must guess. The steps property doc (src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:700-709) says "array" but never warns against the string form, while the content-first flow (write the plan in the reply first, then emit the call) primes pasting the drafted JSON as a string. Repro: emit create_plan with steps as a string containing the JSON array.

(2) resumability-gate evidence phrasing: a context whose findings all came from fresh file reads was rejected at context line 4 ("- Engine choice: src/tool/agent/search.rs:1659 - index path only under ...") as "asserts a symbol is callable/reachable without evidence". The gate (src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:499; tests :2865, :3890) pattern-matches per-line evidence words (verified/probe/probed/observed/measured/confirmed/reproduced/checked) or an 'assumption:' label. The context property (src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:699) lists the words but never states the OPERATIONAL convention: the evidence word must open the SAME line as the claim, e.g. "verified (read src/x.rs:12-40): ..." — so plainly-phrased, genuinely-evidenced findings fail on call one.

Assessment (user asked: too strict or weak instructions?): weak instructions in both spots. The gate's strictness is deliberate and right (SPEC cb44db42, fail-closed against thin plans) — keep it; failure 1 is a typing trap with an error too generic to recover from quickly.

Fix direction: (a) src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs steps property (:700-709): add "steps MUST be a native JSON array — never a string containing JSON"; (b) context property (:699): add the per-line phrasing convention + one passing example bullet ("verified (read src/x.rs:12-40): ..."); (c) src/tool/error_message.rs:87: thread the failing parameter name + expected shape into the type error ("steps: expected array, got string; emit [{\"header\":..., \"body\":...}]") — the schema-validation layer must pass the property name through; (d) optional lenient shim: `steps` arriving as a string that parses as a valid steps JSON array is accepted with a NOTE instead of an error; (e) optionally evaluate gate-side recognition of read-anchored findings without magic words — if not feasible, (a)-(c) alone carry the fix; keep the gate fail-closed either way.

Acceptance: (1) steps-as-string either succeeds via the shim (with note) or errors naming `steps` + the expected shape; (2) a context whose claim lines open with "verified (read ...):" passes the gate first try; (3) an unevidenced "X is reachable from Y" line is still rejected (fail-closed pinned by gate tests at src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:2865/:3890); (4) regression tests for the shim + the description texts (mirror the schema_advertises_* assertion pattern, e.g. src/tool/agent/search.rs:1903); (5) cargo test --workspace green.

Pointers: SPEC cb44db42 (gate rationale, plan b58439f4); memory b69f4a46 superseded 2026-01-15 — the description block moved to src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:685-709 (old src/tool/workflow/ path is stale, G10 lattice moved the workflow tooling under src/app/tool/); live failures: plan 89bbd2a9's first two create_plan calls; update_plan shares the same context gate — mirror the convention into its context property too.

text:
Streamed answer stays plain until the next LLM request

Problem (user-reported live this session, late Jan 2027, watching a streaming answer): the assistant's answer renders as plain text (no markdown) while it streams AND stays plain after the turn completes — headings/lists/code fences apply only once the next request is sent. Repro: ask for a markdown answer (list or code fence); it streams plain; the turn finishes — still plain; send the next prompt — now it is formatted.

Verified mechanism (recon this session, branch wt/mnemo):
- Plain-while-streaming is DELIBERATE: frontend/src/components/chat/Message.tsx:278-291 — MessageImpl's `assistant` case renders raw text while the `streaming` prop is set ("avoid re-parsing markdown on every token"); full markdown (frontend/src/components/chat/Markdown.tsx → lazy MarkdownImpl.tsx, react-markdown) renders only once the entry sits in the transcript WITHOUT `streaming`.
- frontend/src/components/chat/Conversation.tsx:217-222 + 285: while state.streamingText is non-empty a streamingBlock renders that text with `streaming`; it unmounts once flushStreamingText clears the field.
- The turn-end flush DOES exist: frontend/src/hooks/agentEventReducer.ts:1373-1399 reduceFinished calls flushStreamingText (line 1384; reduceError:1437 too); flushStreamingText (frontend/src/hooks/agentState.ts:679-686) pushes the text into the transcript and clears streamingText.

Root-cause suspects (both fit the symptom — untangle which is live):
(a) rAF delta-buffer ordering race: text deltas are buffered and appended per rAF frame (frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStore.ts:560 + :1155; frontend/src/hooks/deltaFlush.ts). A buffered flush landing AFTER the finished event ran flushStreamingText re-populates streamingText → the plain streamingBlock re-mounts and lingers until the next request; reduceStarted (agentEventReducer.ts:200-204) then clears streamingText WITHOUT flushing, dropping that tail.
(b) The activity-log mirror: the answer is also mirrored into activityLog as `answer` entries (appendAnswerEntry, agentEventReducer.ts:257-268, called from reduceTextDelta:283) and the log is NOT cleared at flush (agentState.ts:668-677 — "stays visible until new reasoning starts"), so the thinking box keeps showing the PLAIN answer after the turn ends; check how the reasoning box / InflightBar renders `answer` entries — that may be the copy the user perceives as "still not formatted".

Fix direction: at turn end the answer must render as markdown in the transcript immediately, with no plain remnant in the chat or the thinking box — either drain the rAF buffer before/into the finished flush, or make late deltas not resurrect streamingText after the turn; and/or render the settled answer mirror as markdown once the turn is over (decide per root cause). Keep the per-token plain-text streaming render (a deliberate perf choice); live markdown DURING streaming is a separate optional enhancement.

Acceptance: (1) after a turn finishes the full answer renders markdown with no user action and no plain remnant; (2) text followed by a tool call still flushes ABOVE the tool card (existing contract, agentState.ts:674-677); (3) regression test via the reducer harness (useAgentStore.test.ts pattern): dispatch text_delta(s) → finished with fake timers, including a delta flush landing AFTER finished; assert streamingText === "" AND the transcript's last entry is the full assistant text (must be red before the fix); (4) npm test in frontend/ green.

plan_title: Streamed answer stays plain until the next LLM request — markdown at turn end + late-delta hardening (backlog 076f601e)

text:
One read tool: read_files takes the legacy shape + file_read name redirect

Problem (2026-10-16, user-reported telemetry): "quite a few failures of file_read but not read_files". Probed, verified same day: `file_read` (src/tool/agent/file_read.rs) is registered NOWHERE live — the production agent factory registers only ReadFilesTool (src/agent/factory.rs:1522); every remaining FileReadTool registration is a test fixture (src/runtime/agent.rs cfg(test) registries, src/host/runtime.rs:1052 reviewer-intersection fixture, src/agent/tests.rs, tests/integration/workflow_integration.rs:85). So the observed failures are models calling the retired name from priors and hitting the generic unknown-tool error (src/agent/dispatch.rs:240: `unknown tool '{}'. Available: {}`), plus a hint that CHAINS into the dead name: read_files's invalid-args error for a top-level `path` key points the model at `file_read` (regression `wrong_shape_top_level_path_hints_file_read`, src/tool/agent/read_files.rs:358-373) — a tool that does not exist in production, sending the model straight into the next unknown-tool failure.

Schemas are NOT compatible today: file_read takes {path, start_line?, max_lines?}; read_files takes {files: [{path, start_line?, max_lines?}]}. The 2026-06-03 cross-hints (review: .coding/reviews/2026-06-03-read-tool-args-error-hint-review.md) made shape mix-ups self-correcting, but the name-retirement gaps above remain.

Fix direction (three parts, one landing):
1. read_files one-way shape normalization: a top-level {path, start_line?, max_lines?} object with NO `files` key normalizes to a one-element files array — unambiguous (a valid call always has `files`), zero error surface. Replace the file_read-pointing hint (it redirects to a production-unregistered tool) with the normalization.
2. Legacy-name redirect at the unknown-tool error (src/agent/dispatch.rs:240 and the registry path src/tool/mod.rs:1330): `file_read` → "folded into read_files — call read_files with {\"files\": [{\"path\": …, \"start_line\"?: …, \"max_lines\"?: …}]}", and `file_append` → the file_write equivalent. Keep the existing Available: list.
3. Retire FileReadTool once 1+2 land: delete src/tool/agent/file_read.rs, migrate its test registrations to ReadFilesTool (src/runtime/agent.rs, src/host/runtime.rs:1052, src/agent/tests.rs, tests/integration/workflow_integration.rs). Run the pre-flight import-orphan check (backlog 1ead68c3). Explicitly DO NOT add a silent dispatchable-but-unlisted alias: it hides the footgun, needs new registry machinery, and the habit never unlearns — the redirect lets models recover in one shot and unlearn the name.

Guard for the console rebuild (backlog 51f3be28): the rebuilt console must inherit the Engine factory registry (read_files), never the host test fixture that still registers file_read.

Acceptance: regression tests red-first — (a) read_files called with a top-level {path} SUCCEEDS as a normalized single-file read (red today: invalid-args error); (b) dispatching unregistered file_read returns the redirect text naming read_files + its files shape (red today: plain "unknown tool"); (c) same for file_append. Update `wrong_shape_top_level_path_hints_file_read` to assert the normalization success instead of the hint. Keep the landed cross-hint regressions green otherwise. cargo test --workspace exit 0; tests/boundary.rs green; grep proves no live (non-test) registry registers FileReadTool. Docs sync: PLAN.md's read_files terminology entry (cross-hinting note) and the create_skill.toml comment ("legacy redirect shims") updated to match what actually ships.

Related: memory 2b631328 (PLAN: actionable invalid-args error for mix-ups), review 2026-06-03-read-tool-args-error-hint-review.md, backlog 1ead68c3 (deletion hygiene orphan check), backlog 51f3be28 (console rebuild).

text:
Finish gate: accept exact string-titled vitest tests as regression names

Problem (live case 2026-10-16, plan 3d40e529, branch wt/stream-plain): a bug_fixing plan whose regression test is a vitest it() CANNOT pass the finish gate. Recorded the exact on-disk it() title and finish rejected it twice: first with an appended explanatory suffix ("not found in the code graph and no code file on disk contains the name" — correct rejection, a paraphrase), then with the exact verbatim title ("not found in the code graph even after a forced re-index of 1 file(s) containing the name — the verify step must record the actual test function name" — WRONG rejection, the test is real). Root cause: the gate (src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:2290-2362) accepts a graph symbol OR disk-containment for languages no grammar parses (the matched_unparsed tier, :2304-2326) — but for parsed languages it hard-rejects (:2344-2362), and vitest/Jest tests are STRING-TITLED with anonymous callbacks: it("title", () => {}) produces no symbol (the graph indexes symbol definitions only; titles are string literals). Frontend-only bug plans are structurally unpassable — and Mnemo's own frontend is vitest. The workaround that unblocked 3d40e529 (landed on wt/stream-plain): naming the test body function (regression076f601eLateDeltaSettlesIntoTranscript, frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStore.test.ts ~1919) so the graph indexes it — valid but forced by the gate, and it does not generalize to existing string-titled tests.

Fix direction: extend the disk tier to parsed languages, ONLY for exact test-title acceptance — the recorded name must equal the ENTIRE quoted literal argument of an it( / test( / describe( call in a test file (*.test.*, *.spec.*, tests/, *_test.*, *_tests.*). Accept with the same transparent note style as the unparsable-language tier (:2318-2326). Word-bounded substring stays INSUFFICIENT: suffix paraphrases (the live first failure), partial titles, and comment-only mentions must all still reject — the gate's anti-paraphrase value is the point. Update the error message to name BOTH accepted forms ("record the test function name OR the exact it()/test()/describe() title literal") so the next agent self-corrects in one shot instead of two failed finishes. Implementation hint: the store already keeps each file's raw source + containment rows (src/codegraph/mod.rs:888-897) — the exact-literal check reads the containing file's stored source; the existing forced re-index escalation (backlog 648e0ad5, test finish_force_reindexes_when_meta_fresh_but_symbols_missing at src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:6427) must run BEFORE the title check so a fresh test title resolves on a stale index.

Acceptance: red-first gate tests — an exact full title in an it() call passes (with the transparent note); an appended-suffix paraphrase rejects; a partial title rejects; a comment-only mention rejects; the unparsable-language disk tier still passes. A fixture replicating the 3d40e529 title ("regression (backlog 076f601e): a late text_delta after finished settles into the transcript — never resurrects the plain streaming block") resolves through the new path. cargo test --workspace exit 0; tests/boundary.rs stays green.

Related: review .coding/reviews/2026-10-16-3d40e529-r3-f1-append-branch-delta-review.md (the PASS report the gate was blocking); backlog 648e0ad5 (the forced re-index hardening this builds on); the 2026-10-16 wt/stream-plain commits documenting the live double-rejection.

text:
Steer bookkeeping: "returned to queue" on plain steers is wrong

Problem (user report 2026-10-16): backlog items repeatedly show the note "steered by the user, returned to queue" (live example: item 51f3be28, "App unification on the headless Engine") — the note reads as if the steer requeued the item. User spec: a mid-run steer is a course correction, NOT an abandonment — an item returns to the queue (Pending) ONLY when the user abandons the plan, plus the legitimate agent-exited dead-run recoveries. The "returned to queue" language must never appear on a plain steer.

Verified state (2026-10-16, read of src-tauri/src/ipc/run_all.rs:7140-7219, the steer-resolution match): the status transitions are mostly already right — InFlight + active run → kept InFlight + "kept in flight — the plan stays active, resume to continue" (backlog b83e891f); InFlight + single-dispatch → kept InFlight + pointer restored (0296d448 / cace17a6); Pending (pre-execution) → stays Pending. The defect is the note semantics: the suffix composed at src-tauri/src/ipc/run_all.rs:7148 (`let suffix = format!("{}, returned to queue", iv.reason);`) is ALSO stamped on the Pending arm (:7210-7213, `store.annotate(id, &suffix)`) — a pre-execution item that never left the queue gets annotated "…, returned to queue": factually false and contradicting the spec.

Fix direction: (1) the Pending arm annotates a truthful pre-execution note, e.g. "{reason} (steered before execution — still queued)" — never "returned to queue"; (2) reserve "returned to queue" for actual requeues: plan abandonment (the only user-driven requeue per the spec) and the dead-run recovery arm (:7198-7209, InFlight + run drained — the main-agent-exit case, review round-1 LOW B — legitimate requeue, but its note should lead with the agent-exit cause rather than the steer reason); (3) align the two other requeue composers (src-tauri/src/ipc/run_all.rs:5414, :6821 — spawned/main agent exited while the run was active) so every "returned to queue" note names a real requeue cause; (4) reconcile with the sibling observed bug (memory c5feaec4: a steered chat-driven item stayed InFlight after its plan completed — auto-resolution skipped): keeping steered items in flight is correct per the spec, so the completion-side auto-resolution MUST then actually resolve them — fix both directions together (steer keeps in_flight AND completion resolves steered items).

Acceptance: red-first tests — a steer on a Pending item leaves status Pending with a note that does NOT claim a requeue (assert the note text); a steer on an InFlight item keeps InFlight + the "kept in flight" note (existing tests stay green); the drained-run arm still requeues with an agent-exit-leading note; abandon_plan requeues to Pending; cargo test --workspace exit 0.

Related: memory c5feaec4 (the sibling auto-resolution skip); the fix history in the match arms' comments (b83e891f, 0296d448, cace17a6, 96e2862a); src-tauri/src/ipc/agent.rs:307 (the reason "steered by the user"); src-tauri/src/ipc/state.rs:194 (the note doc); src/app/backlog.rs annotate (status-neutral primitive — correct as-is).

text:
Live browser in every workflow state — web interaction is research

Problem (user report 2026-10-16): interacting with web pages via the live browser tools must be possible during PLANNING and COMPLETE ("done") as well as EXECUTING. Today the workflow-state rules describe the non-executing states as read-only — src/agent/prompt.rs:71 ("PLANNING: read tools + create_plan only — no project mutation without a plan") and :82 ("COMPLETE: read tools + create_plan only — plan any follow-up change") — and the browser family (navigate/click/type/eval/screenshot/DOM snapshot/console logs/multi-page control) is interactive, not read-class. Only web_fetch is explicitly documented as usable in any workflow state for research; revealed browser tools may therefore be filtered or self-blocked in Planning/Complete. Verified (2026-10-16): the group REVEAL is already state-neutral — the test load_tools_allowed_in_every_state_and_inside_skills (src/tool/mod.rs:2826) + the reveal mechanics (src/tool/agent/load_tools.rs:300-332, LoadedGroups, idempotent reveal, permanent for the session). The gap is (a) the per-state tool VISIBILITY/CALLABILITY of the revealed browser tools in Planning/Complete, and (b) the state-rule text, which tells the model web interaction is off-limits there.

Fix direction: (1) make the browser tool group research-class in the per-state visibility layer — visible/callable in Planning, Executing, Reviewing, and Complete once revealed (the reveal is permanent for the session); (2) update the two state-rule strings at src/agent/prompt.rs:71/:82 so Planning/Complete read "read tools + create_plan + web interaction (web_fetch / the revealed browser tools)" — the model must not self-block; (3) keep the existing safety levels unchanged (approvals still gate dangerous navigations/downloads exactly as today); (4) the `browser` cargo feature (chromiumoxide) and the Windows-only WebView2 own-tab tooling stay as-is — this item is about STATE gating only, not the feature gate.

Acceptance: per-state fixtures — load_tools("browser") + a browser call succeeds in each of Planning/Executing/Reviewing/Complete (a fake-table browser tool suffices; no real Chromium needed); the two prompt.rs state-rule strings carry the web-interaction carve-out; cargo test --workspace exit 0; the feature-gated run cargo test --features browser green (no pull-request job compiles the browser tree — plain cargo test never does, so this is the run that catches breakage).

Related: src/tool/mod.rs:2826 (the state-neutral reveal test this builds on), src/agent/prompt.rs:71/:82 (the state-rule strings), the project constitution's browser-feature note (cargo test --features browser for the chromiumoxide tree), the sanctioned Windows-only WebView2 Browser tab exception (unchanged by this).

text:
Finish should tick appended review-fix steps

Problem (2026-10-21, live case plan 8813e7ab): a plan that goes through review rounds ends Complete with its appended fix steps still rendered as open checkboxes. `.coding/plans/8813e7ab.md` shows `- [x]` on steps 1-7 and `- [ ]` on steps 8-13 — the six steps `update_plan append=true` added in Reviewing for the review findings H1-H4, L1-L4 and the verify/commit step — even though the work shipped (commits 36e7a74, e2729c8, 6219ec9 on wt/mnemo) and review round 3 returned `## Verdict: PASS` (.coding/reviews/2026-10-21-8813e7ab-toolcard-labels-review-round3.md). Anyone reading the plan frame sees six open items on a completed plan.

Cause: `complete_step` is hidden in the Reviewing state by design (a reviewer-driven fix must not rewrite plan progress), and the sanctioned fix-scoping path (`update_plan` with `append=true`) produces steps that stay unchecked "through the exit" per the workflow lifecycle text.

Fix direction: when a plan finishes — the `finish` tool's handler on the transition into Complete — mark every still-unchecked step of that plan as done in the frame, or move appended review-fix steps into a distinct `## Review fixes (done)` section with its own state. Keep every step's TEXT (the frame is the crash-resumption document; never drop them). Anchors: `src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs` (the `finish` and `update_plan` handlers) and `src/app/workflow/plan_file.rs` (the plan-frame writer that renders `- [x] N.` / `- [ ] N.`); the lifecycle sentence that documents the current behaviour is in `src/agent/prompt.rs` (WORKFLOW_LIFECYCLE, the Reviewing-adjacent text).

Acceptance: a plan whose listed steps are all complete, with two steps appended during Reviewing, run to Complete must render with no unchecked step (or the appended pair under the done section), and `current_plan` / the plan pane must agree with the frame. Regression test in the plan-tool tests (plan.rs / plan_file.rs): finish a plan carrying appended unchecked steps, assert no `- [ ]` remains; the red-check on today's code shows the six `- [ ]` lines.

Pointers: memory SPEC "chat tool cards — one human headline per run" (plan 8813e7ab) and its round-3 PASS report; `.coding/plans/8813e7ab.md` itself is the reproduction fixture.

text:
OpenSpec support: current-state specs, spec deltas on plans, schemas and a Settings > Specs page

Spec: .coding/design/openspec-support.md (read it first; written 2026-11-04 with the user).

Adopt OpenSpec's file formats, not its tool: current-state specs in openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md (Requirement/SHALL + WHEN/THEN scenarios), plans carry ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED/RENAMED spec deltas, closing a plan merges them and writes an OpenSpec archive folder (close is gated on clean deltas). Support OpenSpec schemas (schema.yaml artifacts, templates, instructions, config.yaml context/rules) as plan sections and dispatch gates, with a Settings > Specs page to pick, add, fork and edit schemas. Backlog gets a "Plan this" button. Start with the dispatch-routing and tier-ladder capabilities. Plan after unified tiers (87932c46); three open questions are at the end of the spec.
